title: Florida Anti-Tampering Act
text: Any person who with intent to cause injury to any person or with intent to cause economic loss to any person places or causes to be placed a harmful object in a consumer product or a container of a consumer product or on the premises of a retail merchant with intent that the object be part of the consumer product, or any person who without the knowledge, intent, or authorization of the manufacturer, retailer, or any other person, places or causes to be placed a harmful object in a consumer product or a container of a consumer product or tampers with a consumer product, or any person who communicates to any person a threat that a harmful object has been placed in a consumer product or a container of a consumer product knowing that such threat is false, shall be guilty of a felony of the first degree.
summary: Criminalizes intentional tampering with consumer products or false communications about tampering. Establishes felony-level penalties for tampering or communicating false threats about product tampering.

title: Unfair or Deceptive Trade Practices
text: (1) Unfair or deceptive acts or practices, methods, acts, or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are declared to be unlawful. (2) In determining whether an act, method, act, or practice is unfair or deceptive, the factors that may be considered include: (a) Whether the defendant has represented, expressly or by implication, that a product or service has sponsorship, approval, characteristics, ingredients, uses, benefits, or quantities which it does not have or that a person has a sponsorship, approval, status, affiliation, or connection which he does not have.
summary: Establishes the foundational prohibition against unfair or deceptive trade practices in Florida commerce. Forms the basis for consumer protection claims including misrepresentation and deceptive business conduct.

title: Copyright Owners and Performing Rights Societies
text: (1) DEFINITIONS.—As used in this section: (a) 'Copyright owner' means any person who owns a copyright or any exclusive copyright rights in and to any musical composition. (b) 'Performing rights society' means any person, entity, or association which licenses or distributes performing rights to copyrighted musical compositions on behalf of copyright owners. (c) 'Proprietor' means any person who operates a business or other establishment in which copyrighted music is performed or presented. (2) PROHIBITED PRACTICES.—A performing rights society shall not enter into a royalty contract with a proprietor unless such performing rights society provides the proprietor with written notice including the royalty rate schedule, duration of license, availability of copyright, toll-free verification number, and proprietor's right to obtain license forms.
summary: Protects business proprietors from unfair licensing practices by performing rights societies. Requires written disclosure 72 hours before contract execution with rates, terms, and copyright verification rights.

title: Actions Based Upon Use of a Creation Not Protected Under Federal Copyright Law
text: Any person who is injured by a violation of this part by another person may bring an action for damages, including an action based upon use of a creation that is not protected under federal copyright law. The burden shall be upon the plaintiff to establish that the creation is not protected under federal copyright law.
summary: Creates private right of action for unfair trade practices involving creations not protected by federal copyright law. Bridges gap for state-law remedies when federal copyright protection unavailable.

title: Unfair or Deceptive Acts or Practices; Vehicles
text: Unfair or deceptive acts or practices involving the sale or lease of a vehicle include, but are not limited to: (1) Representing that a vehicle has been repaired, serviced, reconditioned, or overhauled when such is not the fact; (2) Representing the condition of a vehicle with respect to repairs needed; (3) Misrepresenting the mileage on a vehicle; (4) Misrepresenting the ownership history of a vehicle; (5) Failing to disclose known defects that materially affect the use, value, or safety of the vehicle.
summary: Prohibits unfair or deceptive trade practices specific to vehicle sales and leasing. Common violations include hiding defects, falsifying mileage, and misrepresenting ownership history.

title: Equity Actions; Removing Clouds on Title
text: Any person in possession of, or having the right to possession of, real property, or any estate or interest therein, against which any outstanding claim or encumbrance, arising out of any written instrument, deed, will, record, or other evidence of title is apparent on the face of the record, by which the title to such real property, estate, or interest is, or may be, clouded, may bring an action in equity in the circuit court of the county in which such real property is located.
summary: Establishes civil equity procedures for quiet title actions to establish clear ownership and remove title defects (clouds). Courts can determine owner, award possession, and impose costs.

title: Short Title - Residential Tenancies Act
text: This part shall be known and may be cited as the 'Residential Tenancies Act.'
summary: Establishes short title for Chapter 83, Part II, governing all landlord-tenant relationships in Florida residential rental properties.

title: Deposit Money or Advance Rent; Duty of Landlord and Tenant
text: (1) The landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit exceeding one month's rent for tenancies of one year or less, or two month's rent for tenancies exceeding one year. (2) All money paid as a security deposit shall be held in trust by the landlord in an interest-bearing account in a state or federally chartered bank, savings association, or credit union. (3) The landlord shall pay the tenant interest at a rate equal to the rate paid by the depository but not less than 2 percent per annum for any part held more than 12 months. (4) Within 30 days after tenancy ends, the landlord shall return the deposit plus interest, minus itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
summary: Requires landlords to handle security deposits in interest-bearing accounts and return them with interest within 30-45 days. Caps deposits at one/two month's rent and limits deductions.

title: Landlord's Obligation to Maintain Premises
text: (1) The landlord shall at all times during the tenancy maintain the dwelling unit in habitable condition meaning premises are free from hazardous defects, capable of safely occupying human beings, in compliance with applicable building, housing, and health codes. (2) The landlord shall maintain structural components, electrical, plumbing, heating, cooling and other facilities, safe locks and security devices, safe ingress and egress, hot and cold running water, and heating facilities capable of heating habitable rooms to at least 68 degrees Fahrenheit.
summary: Requires landlords to maintain properties in habitable condition per building/health codes. Tenants may withhold rent, terminate lease, or sue for damages if landlord breaches.

title: Landlord's Access to Dwelling Unit
text: The landlord may enter the dwelling unit only: (a) In case of emergency; (b) To make ordinary repairs, decorations, alterations or improvements; (c) To show the dwelling unit to prospective or existing tenants, purchasers, or lenders; (d) For inspection purposes as permitted by law. The landlord shall provide the tenant with notice of intent to enter not less than 12 hours before the entry.
summary: Landlords have limited entry rights requiring 12-hour notice except in emergencies. Protects tenant privacy and quiet enjoyment of premises.

title: Retaliatory Conduct
text: (1) A landlord may not take reprisal by increasing rent, decreasing services, or threatening such action by reason that the tenant has complained to the landlord or governmental agency of noncompliance materially affecting health and safety, or exercised rights granted by law. (2) Acts within 6 months of such conduct constitute prima facie evidence of retaliation including increasing rent, decreasing services, or bringing possession actions. (3) If landlord proves by clear and convincing evidence the action would have been taken regardless of tenant's complaint, the presumption of retaliation may be rebutted.
summary: Prohibits landlord retaliation against tenants reporting violations. Creates presumption of retaliation if adverse action taken within 6 months; landlord must prove legitimate reason.

title: Foreclosure of Mortgages and Statutory Liens
text: Any mortgagee or other lienor entitled to foreclose shall do so by action in which the mortgagee shall make the mortgagor a party defendant and obtain judgment of foreclosure and sale or deficiency judgment as provided in this chapter. All such actions shall be brought in circuit court of the county in which the property is located, and the action shall be an action in equity. (2) In any foreclosure action, the defendant may assert any defense or counterclaim arising out of the transaction.
summary: All mortgage foreclosures are equity actions in circuit court. Borrowers may defend and assert counterclaims. Establishes due-process framework protecting borrower rights.

title: Definitions - Construction Defects
text: 'Construction defect' means a deficiency in design, specifications, surveying, planning, supervision, observation, construction, repair, alteration, or remodeling of real property arising from: (a) Defective material, products, or components; (b) Failure to comply with applicable building codes; (c) Design failure to meet professional standards; or (d) Failure to construct per accepted trade standards and good workmanship.
summary: Defines construction defects broadly including defective materials, code violations, design failures, and substandard workmanship. Applies to both residential and commercial property.

title: Construction Liens
text: Every person that provides labor, materials, or services for the improvement of real property shall have a lien on the property improved for the contract price of the labor, materials, or services furnished. This lien shall be effective from the date of the furnishing of the labor, materials, or services.
summary: Grants construction workers and suppliers automatic liens on real property to secure payment for work performed. Provides foundational lien rights for contractors and subcontractors.

title: Statute of Limitations - General Civil Actions
text: (1) An action for breach of contract, express or implied, including actions for payment of debt arising from contract and actions for specific performance shall be commenced within the later of: (a) Five years after the right of action accrues; or (b) For fraud, within four years after fraud is discovered or should have been discovered. (2) An action for negligence shall be commenced within the later of: (a) Four years after right of action accrues; or (b) Two years after injury is discovered or should have been discovered with due diligence.
summary: Sets strict time limits for filing lawsuits. Contract disputes: 5 years. Fraud: 4 years. Negligence: 2 years from injury discovery. Missing deadlines bars claims forever.

title: Comparative Negligence
text: (1) In all actions for negligence or strict liability, the fact that the plaintiff was guilty of comparative negligence shall not bar recovery if plaintiff was not as negligent as the defendant. (2) The court shall direct the jury to return a special verdict in percentages of negligence contributed to the accident by each party. (3) Any negligence chargeable to the plaintiff shall diminish proportionately the allowance to the plaintiff.
summary: Modified comparative negligence: if plaintiff is less than 50% at fault, they recover reduced by their percentage. If 50%+ at fault, no recovery.

title: Insurer's Duty to Acknowledge Communications and Investigate Claims
text: (1) An insurer shall acknowledge receipt of a claim within 24 business days of receipt. (2) An insurer shall begin investigation of a claim immediately upon receipt of notice of loss and shall investigate all claims with reasonable diligence. (3) An insurer shall assign a specific individual to be the contact person and shall provide claimant with name, title, office address, telephone number, and electronic mail address.
summary: Requires insurers to acknowledge claims within 24 business hours, assign an adjuster, begin investigation immediately, and maintain reasonable communication.

title: Notice of Property Insurance Claim
text: (1) Policyholders must notify insurers of loss within one year from date of loss. (2) Notice may be written or oral per policy provisions; email, phone, or mail acceptable. (3) Notice should identify property, location, date of loss, and nature of damage. (4) Failure to provide timely notice may bar claim if insurer suffered prejudice.
summary: Requires one-year notice deadline for property claims. Notice can be oral or written. Late notice may bar claim only if insurer proves prejudice.

title: Valued Policy Law
text: If a policy of insurance valued in excess of one hundred dollars shall have been issued on any real or personal property and said property shall be wholly destroyed, without criminal fault on the part of the insured, the insurer shall be liable for the full amount specified in the policy.
summary: For total property loss, insurers must pay full face amount stated in policy regardless of actual value. Does not apply to partial losses or if fraud committed.

title: Sinkhole Loss Coverage and Catastrophic Ground Collapse
text: An insurer may exclude or limit coverage for sinkhole loss or catastrophic ground collapse; if not excluded, coverage is provided. An insurer may require geological investigation and testing to determine if loss is sinkhole-related. Testing must follow scientific standards established by Florida Department of Financial Services.
summary: Sinkhole coverage is optional. If included, claims subject to geological testing per state standards. Disputes over sinkhole causation trigger alternative dispute resolution.
